evals.prompt: Here is an export of our last 60 Instagram captions and 12 blog posts (folder: ./corpus, with social/ and long_form/ subfolders). Figure out our brand voice and write it up so a freelancer could write for us next week without reading everything. Save the guideline as voice-guideline.md in the output directory and the prompt blocks as voice-prompt-blocks.md.
assertions: voice-guideline.md and voice-prompt-blocks.md exist in the outputs directory
Stats were produced by running scripts/text_stats.py (a stats.json exists in data/ or work/) rather than estimated by reading
Social and long-form are documented as separate systems with their own length, emoji/hashtag and CTA figures — not one averaged voice
Every rule carries an evidence count (e.g. '41/60 captions') or named corpus IDs
Statements are labeled Rule / Variation (with trigger) / Exception per the 70% / 30-70% / 30% thresholds
There is one voice prompt block per channel, compact, containing verbatim hook and CTA examples in the source language
The document ends with a coverage section naming what the corpus did not contain (ads, web, other languages, dates)

evals.prompt: Our Turkish e-commerce brand runs Meta ads and posts on Instagram, mostly in Turkish with some English. I've put 30 ad texts and 45 captions in ./texts as a JSONL (fields: text, channel, language, engagement). Tell me what our voice actually is — hooks, CTAs, how we frame discounts, emoji habits — and give me something I can paste into a prompt so generated ad copy sounds like us. Output to the output directory.
assertions: text_stats.py was run on the JSONL and its per-channel aggregates (cta_rate, hook_distribution, mean_emoji_count, mean_chars) are cited
Verbatim Turkish hooks and CTAs are quoted as evidence (not paraphrased or translated), with rule text in English
Offer framing (percentage vs absolute vs threshold) and urgency devices are documented per channel with counts
Language mix is reported per channel with counts and the prompt block states which language to write in and where English is used
Engagement was joined honestly: any 'top-tier posts do X' claim states the sample size and confounds

A compact voice prompt block for ads (and one for social) exists following the template: Voice / Attributes / Person-formality / Hook / Structure / Length / CTA / Offer framing / Emoji / Hashtags / Language / Never

evals.prompt: Make this generated LinkedIn post sound like our company. Our real posts are in ./our-posts (20 .txt files). Draft: 'We are thrilled to announce that our innovative platform now supports advanced analytics! Reach out to learn more.' Save the rewrite and a short explanation of what you changed and why to rewrite.md in the output directory.
assertions: rewrite.md exists in the outputs directory with the rewritten post
The corpus was actually analyzed (stats run + reading pass) before rewriting; the explanation cites specific corpus patterns (hook type, person, length, CTA wording, emoji/hashtag policy)
The rewrite's stats (length, hook type, person, CTA presence, emoji/hashtag counts) are compared against the corpus range, not just asserted to match
Generic-announcement tells ('thrilled to announce', 'innovative', 'reach out to learn more') are replaced only where the corpus shows the brand does not use them, with evidence
